pass_a_gloss: Shame despised; sword and fire divide earthy/heavenly; good hatred frees perfect love.
pass_b_english: Despising shame, Jesus endured the cross — 'who for the joy set before him endured the cross, despising shame.' (Hebrews 12:2) Let us too despise the shame of men. For he brings not peace but a sword — dividing son from father, daughter from mother — that the Word, sharper than any two-edged sword, may divide in us the earthy image from the heavenly, soul from spirit, joints from marrow. 'I came to cast fire on the earth — and how I wish it were kindled! I have a baptism to be baptized with.' (Matthew 10:34–36) Hate then father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters — yea, and one's own soul too — hating lawfully what hinders godliness: a good hatred, that perfect love may remain toward God alone (Hebrews 4:12) (Luke 12:49–50) (Luke 14:26) (John 12:25).
